# Persist a single editable region

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Choose a permitted HTML block and formatting policy, then retain one saved content authority through controlled echoes, edit mode and recovery.

[Documentation home](../INDEX.md)

## Single-block editing

`EditableText` owns one formatted block with hard breaks. It is controlled React UI with no SPFx provider requirement. Native SPFx AMD resources supply its UI labels. Read mode renders safe content; Edit loads the private editor on demand. The caller owns the saved HTML and reflects user changes into `value`. Mounting, loading external content and changing configuration never save normalized HTML automatically.

Import `EditableText`, `EditableTextProps`, `EditableTextBlock`, `EditableTextChangeData`, `EditableTextStrings`, `EditableTextColorNames` and `EditableTextStringsOverride` from `@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit`, `/controls` or `/controls/editable-text`. These resolve to the same public implementation and types. There are no public engine, AST, codec, toolbar slot or plugin exports.

### React usage

Mount the complete recipes below under the application's existing FluentProvider and document's Griffel RendererProvider.

React 17's `useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)` interoperates with the legacy React ref API; application absence values use `undefined`. No SPFx hook/provider is required. Share the host's existing Fluent/Griffel peers; the control creates no provider or renderer. The host sets theme, direction, popup target document and renderer target document, including iframe/secondary-document scenarios.

The stable native `div` owns a `p` or H1–H4 region. Place it in a block-capable container, outside labels, buttons, triggers and other inline-only slots. It is not a general replacement for arbitrary inline slot content. Use [FormattedText](../api/controls/formatted-text.md) for read-only Markdown/JSX rendering.

### Choose a block policy

`EditableTextBlock` is `'p' | 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'`. `EditableTextProps` inherits the supported React native div attributes/events, `className` and consumer `style`; these and the forwarded `ref` target the same outer div in both modes. The control owns children, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `contentEditable`, `suppressContentEditableWarning`, `defaultValue`, `role` and `dir`. Use FluentProvider direction rather than a control `dir` prop. Native `onChange` is replaced by the domain callback below.

Runtime validation throws `TypeError` for invalid strings, mode, callback, accessible Edit name or block policy. TypeScript cannot guarantee nonempty string values. An empty allowed array, unsupported runtime member (including H5/H6), or explicit default outside the set is invalid. Equivalent arrays such as `['h2', 'h4']` and `['h4', 'h2', 'h2']` represent the same membership.

For example, `<h2>Project</h2>` under `allowedBlocks={['p']}` renders a paragraph. Stored input remains the original H2 until a user edit publishes a paragraph. This is valid policy conversion, not an import error or fallback. Read and Edit initialization, paste, external replacement and reset use the same finite policy. Font size, emphasis, color and line spacing are independent of the semantic block choice.

### UI dictionaries and migration

`locale` has been removed in this major API migration. Configure the package's native SPFx localized resources in the consuming solution; SPFx selects one culture when loading its AMD module. Changing `pageContext` or a browser locale at runtime does not reload that module. The 50 canonical translator catalogs remain package build inputs. Outside the SPFx loader, the host must provide an explicit resource-module adapter even when supplying a complete custom dictionary.

Use `strings={{ bold: 'Strong', colorNames: { red: 'Danger' } }}` for per-instance overrides. `EditableTextStrings` is a complete dictionary and `EditableTextStringsOverride` is partial except for its independently partial `colorNames`. `EditableTextColorNames` has only public semantic fields and no private editor/AST dependency. `EditableTextStringsOverride.colorNames` overrides individual entries; its omission inherits all names. Complete dictionaries require every label, formatter and color; partial dictionaries inherit omitted/undefined fields. Empty strings are retained as explicit values. Direct `placeholder` takes precedence, including `''` to suppress the hint. Direct ARIA props alone name the textbox; dictionary hints cannot satisfy Edit's accessible-name requirement.

Formatter callbacks receive heading levels 1–4, numeric line spacing, a translated label plus literal shortcut, or a mixed-state label. They return UI strings, run during rendering and must be pure. Defaults use the selected native catalog's templates, preserving literal inserted labels and shortcuts. Replacing a dictionary updates toolbar/color/hint/loading/recovery labels on the existing editor without publishing `onChange`, changing author content, resetting selection or clearing undo history. Two instances can use different dictionaries under the same native culture. The sample dictionary selector demonstrates native labels, a complete Italian `EditableTextStrings` dictionary (all callbacks and semantic color names), and partial project-label overrides on the same subject. Theme and direction remain host concerns.

### Color picker and theme colors

The circular Fluent SwatchPicker contains vertically stacked Automatic, Theme colors and Standard colors sections, each with a horizontal wrapping row of swatches. Every swatch has a localized name and Tooltip available on pointer hover and keyboard focus; the accessible name matches that name. Theme colors describe roles rather than promising a fixed black/blue value. The same picker and names are available in the toolbar overflow.

The default light-theme palette follows the reference order: 12 Theme colors and 10 Standard colors. The values come exclusively from foreground tokens; fixed `color-mix(in srgb, …)` recipes provide intermediate tones. Their appearance follows the current Fluent theme and may differ from the older Office reference palette, particularly its cyan, blue and purple.

The accepted protocol retains four earlier colors: `orange` (dark-orange foreground 3), `teal`, `pink` and `brown` (their palette foreground 2). These remain valid in saved content and appear in the picker while selected, without expanding the default palette. All 26 IDs use stable `wps-color-<id>` markers; derived tones never save CSS expressions or resolved colors in the document.

Colors resolve from the active FluentProvider theme supplied by the host. Duplicate resolved colors are collapsed while preserving the currently selected identity and Automatic. For example, default dark-theme red and dark red coincide, so only one is offered at a time; both protocol IDs remain valid. Automatic removes only the color override, preserving emphasis, size and block formatting. Existing primary/subtle/brand content remains valid. No custom HEX/RGB color picker is provided.

### Controlled updates, history and composition

Canonical echoes preserve the current selection and history. Actual external source replacement (`value`/`fallbackText`) establishes a new undo baseline. A membership change reconciles the live draft, retaining the editor, text, marks and valid selection while resetting undo, even if the current block is still admitted. Reordering/duplicates do not reset it. Changing only `defaultBlock` preserves history and a nonempty admitted block. Placeholder and dictionary updates preserve the draft, selection and history. None of these configuration operations emits a callback.

During IME composition the latest committed policy applies after composition. An Edit→Read transition finishes pending Edit input with the current policy and latest provided callback, including when all three change in the same render. If Read omits its optional callback, only that final pending Edit flush uses the last committed Edit callback. Read then originates no changes. A configuration-only exit publishes nothing. Effective deletion emits `{ html: '', text: '' }`; formatting an empty document prepares future typing without publishing empty markup.

### HTML and editing limits

Canonical content consists of one p/H1–H4 block, text, `br`, strong/emphasis/underline and the supported semantic formatting markers. Enter and Shift+Enter insert hard breaks; multiple incoming blocks normalize into the one region. Bold/italic/underline commands and Ctrl/Cmd+B/I/U retain selection and provide undo boundaries. A caret-only inline formatting command affects the whole nonempty region. Clear formatting retains the block type. The editor supports size 8–96 px, finite line spacing and theme-derived color choices; H5/H6, lists, links, images, Markdown conversion and multi-paragraph documents are outside the public editing model. Unsupported wrappers may contribute safe text; unsafe embedded/executable subtrees are discarded. Unsupported markup is never injected as raw HTML.

The persisted protocol is shared with [WebPartShell titles](#title-authority-and-html-protocol): existing `wps-*` semantic classes, escaped content, mark order and accepted legacy size/color imports are retained. Color IDs resolve against the current Fluent theme rather than storing arbitrary HEX colors. HTML input and output are limited to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes with parsing depth 32. Unrecoverable imports use literal fallback. An oversized live draft stays visible with an error and suppresses publication, without partial/truncated callbacks. Resolve the draft or replace its source before persisting it.

### Caller-owned SPFx persistence

Render this content under an initialized matching SPFx provider, for example [WebPartShell](../api/controls/web-part-shell.md). The existing hooks remain in the caller. They are not dependencies of EditableText itself.

`setProperties` shallow-merges partial property updates through the provider's host integration. This example preserves a plain search value beside canonical HTML. Empty HTML remains authoritative after reload. Property metadata, persistence permissions and any explicit saving workflow belong to the host application. Normalization alone writes neither property.

## Web part title authority and editing

### Card appearance and title position

`WebPartShellAppearance` uses the native Fluent `CardProps['appearance']` values: `subtle`, `filled`, `filled-alternative` and `outline`. The Shell default is `subtle`, which deliberately renders no Card. `WebPartShellSize` follows `CardProps['size']`: `small`, `medium` (default) and `large`. `WebPartShellTitlePosition` accepts `outside` (default) and `inside`; title and actions always move as one header. All three are optional React props. They add no persisted keys to `IWebPartShellProperties`, and mapping them to a consumer's Property Pane is optional. With subtle, size and titlePosition have no visual effect.

The Card uses native size (medium by default), vertical layout, visual styling and `focusMode="off"`. Small/medium/large supply native inner padding and gap of 8/12/16px respectively, together with the corresponding Fluent border radius. It does not add selection or a focus trap; child controls retain their own interaction. Its native overflow policy applies to caller-owned content. The title toolbar and menus retain their existing Fluent portals and owner document. Native root attributes/events, `className`, caller `style` and ref still target the outer Shell div, not the Card. No automatic accessible-name association between the custom title and Card is added.

Shell `padding` remains the outer inset around the whole composition. A visible Card independently supplies the selected size's native inner padding and header/body gap. `padding="none"` removes the outer inset, not the Card's inner padding. The outer header-to-Card gap remains the existing medium Shell gap for every Card size. Hiding the header removes its gap; Card inner padding remains.

Changing size preserves the Card, header/editor/actions and body state. Changing among filled, filled-alternative and outline keeps Card/body state. Changing titlePosition keeps the Card/body but can recreate the header, its actions and the title editor. Switching between subtle and a Card can recreate body content as its React ancestry changes. Consumers should keep state that must survive those structural changes outside that subtree. No title properties are reset by these presentation changes; removing an active title editor retains its established pending-edit flush behavior.

### Surface, theme and lifecycle

Auto surface selects application when the SPFx Microsoft 365 SDK is present or the guarded optional `legacyPageContext.pageLayoutType` equals exactly `SingleWebPartAppPage`. SDK presence is enough before asynchronous context acquisition completes. Missing, malformed or unknown legacy metadata falls back to section; the legacy field is not a stable detection guarantee. Use `surface="application"` when an application host lacks that signal. Surface detection uses neither viewport width nor manifest/form-factor inference, REST or polling.

Section adds zero automatic padding and a transparent background, including the Fluent wrapper. Application uses the existing medium spacing (12px) below 640px container inline-size and large spacing (16px) from 640px. Explicit padding wins. The container query measures the shell root, separately from its padded content; it is not a viewport breakpoint. Layout uses natural height and a wrapping title/action header. The shell adds no scroll lock, sticky header or SharePoint canvas sizing.

Without Card, header and body are separated by `gap.medium` (12px with the default Fluent theme) in every surface, including SharePoint sections. This gap is independent of outer padding. With Card, the header is separated from the Card or from its inner body according to titlePosition. `showTitle=false` removes the complete header, its actions and its gap in either placement. Content remains mounted when title visibility changes. An empty title with showTitle=true still permits actions and the Edit placeholder.

The title and header actions are vertically centered within their wrapping row using `alignItems.center`.

Theme tokens merge host, then the nearest ancestor Fluent theme, then the explicit theme override. Missing partial ancestor tokens come from the host; without a host theme, the hook supplies a light fallback. Direction resolves explicit `dir`, then an actual ancestor FluentProvider, then SPFx `cultureInfo.isRightToLeft`. A low-level Fluent context without the provider theme-class context does not establish ancestor direction. The shell supplies `targetDocument` from `instance.context.domElement.ownerDocument` and inherits Griffel's renderer. The host must supply a renderer for that document, including iframe hosts; the shell creates no renderer.

Ordinary same-instance rerenders preserve application content and actions. A different `instanceId` resets the keyed runtime subtree. Hiding the title unmounts the header/editor/actions while preserving children; showing it creates a fresh header. Emptying a visible title keeps its actions. Title Read/Edit changes mount/destroy only the editor. Appearance and placement have the structural remount boundaries described above. The existing SPFx provider owns service readiness, instance isolation and subscriptions; dispose the React root in the web part's `onDispose`.

### Title authority and HTML protocol

With undefined `titleHTML`, `title` is literal text rendered as H2. A defined empty `titleHTML` means an empty title even when the old plain title is nonempty. Empty/whitespace-only documents render no heading in Read; Edit shows an unsaved placeholder. Recoverable imported HTML is normalized in memory without property writes. Unrecoverable input uses the literal plain fallback and an Edit-mode warning. Mounting, theme changes, focus and selection do not rewrite properties.

The private document contains one H1–H4 or Normal paragraph block, with text and hard breaks. Enter and Shift+Enter insert a hard break in that block outside IME composition. Multiblock paste joins block boundaries with hard breaks and uses the first supported block's format. These are V1 choices rather than a promise of exact native SharePoint editor parity.

Canonical HTML uses `p`, `h1`–`h4`, `strong`, `em`, `u`, `span` and `br`, escaped text, stable semantic classes and deterministic nesting (`strong` → `em` → `u` → `span`). Read renders validated React nodes and does not inject original HTML or load Tiptap.

Import accepts `b`/`i`, the observed legacy `fontSizeXLarge` alias as 20px, and `fontColorBlue` as the semantic brand role (no identical RGB guarantee). A supported unitless native `line-height` on a supported block can be imported; other inline styles, URLs, event handlers and unknown classes are discarded. Harmless wrappers flatten to text; active/embedded/form/media subtrees are removed. Persisted classes are protocol markers under scoped Griffel rules, not Griffel hashes. Theme changes alter tokens without rewriting HTML.

Read and Edit share the official Fluent typography recipes, including font family and weight. The font-size picker reflects inherited theme sizes; explicit `wps-size-N` and `wps-line-N` values remain authoritative. Existing titles without overrides adopt these presets without a property write or HTML migration; imported native `line-height:1.4` remains an explicit override. Semantic heading levels and visual presets are associated by this control, not automatically by Fluent.

Input and canonical output are limited to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes; parser nesting is limited to depth 32. Input that exceeds a limit or would exceed the canonical byte limit uses the safe fallback. An oversized editor draft stays visible with a recoverable size error; neither title property is patched until the draft fits. There is no implicit truncation. Leaving Edit discards an unsaved oversized draft when the editor is destroyed; previously saved properties remain authoritative.

### Title editor localization

The title delegates its color picker to `EditableText`. See [Color picker and theme colors](#color-picker-and-theme-colors) for palette IDs, theme resolution, accessible swatch names and Automatic behavior. The picker uses the shell's effective Fluent theme, including host, ancestor and explicit overrides.

Native SPFx AMD modules supply the Shell naming and common editor labels from the 50 canonical SharePoint UI-culture catalogs. Configure the package localized resources in the consuming solution; SPFx selects the modules when loading the page. Changing the instance pageContext or regional culture at runtime does not replace an already loaded native module. Hosts outside the SPFx loader need an explicit module adapter.

`WebPartShellStrings` contains `titleEditorLabel` (the actual title textbox's accessible name) and `titlePlaceholder` (the literal empty title hint). Set `strings?: Partial<WebPartShellStrings>` to override either independently. Set `titleEditorStrings?: EditableTextStringsOverride` to customize common toolbar, swatch, formatter, loading and recovery labels using the [EditableText dictionary contract](#ui-dictionaries-and-migration). Omitted/undefined fields inherit native labels; an empty titlePlaceholder suppresses the hint. A nonempty titleEditorLabel remains required in Edit. A complete WebPartShellStrings value has both fields.

For example: `<WebPartShell instance={this} strings={{ titleEditorLabel: 'Section heading', titlePlaceholder: 'Add a heading' }} titleEditorStrings={{ bold: 'Strong', colorNames: { red: 'Danger' } }} />`. Both dictionaries are per instance. Shell naming takes precedence over the editor dictionary's generic placeholder; the editor dictionary cannot replace the shell-owned accessible name. Live replacement retains the editor view, draft, marks, selection, undo and stored author content without publishing properties. Direction follows the existing dir/ancestor/SPFx contract separately.

Translation key/placeholder checks and browser tests establish resource coverage and UI binding; they do not certify native-speaker linguistic quality. Authenticated SharePoint and screen-reader checks remain separate from local browser results.

### Editing and recovery

All author UI uses Fluent UI 9: floating Popover/Toolbar, heading Dropdown, validated font-size Combobox, finite theme SwatchPicker, spacing Menu, clear formatting, Overflow commands, Spinner and MessageBar. Tiptap manages only the contenteditable engine. All control-owned labels, tooltips, accessible names, placeholders and recovery messages use native SPFx labels and the instance dictionaries. Browser spellcheck remains available; author text and consumer-owned content are never translated.

With a selected text range, inline formatting applies to that range. Without a text selection, bold, italic, underline, font size, color and Clear apply to the entire title while preserving the caret position. Ctrl/Cmd+B/I/U follows the same scope. Mixed emphasis becomes uniform on the first action and is removed on the next action; toolbar state describes the whole title at a caret. Color and size changes preserve each text run's unrelated overrides. An empty title stores formatting for subsequent typing without publishing empty-title properties.

Each formatting gesture forms one undo boundary. Clear removes targeted inline marks and block spacing overrides while keeping text and heading level. Heading and spacing already address the title's single block. Popup commands preserve the original caret/range and return editor focus where appropriate; keyboard Tab remains available. Icon buttons and toggles use the same medium size; heading and font-size selectors use small size and are vertically centered with compact widths. The toolbar fits its control content, keeps a theme-token gap between heading and font size, and moves commands into Fluent Overflow when space is limited. Format painter is intentionally absent in V1. Escape does not revert content already published.

One editor view exists per Edit session. Effective document transactions publish one merged `{ title, titleHTML }` patch, preserving other application properties; plain search text comes from the same validated document with breaks/whitespace normalized. Canonical echoes preserve selection/history. A real external title replacement updates the existing view, clamps its selection and establishes fresh history so Undo cannot restore the preceding external version. Theme/direction changes leave history intact.

During IME composition, external replacements wait. The latest pending replacement applies after composition only if a newer local edit has not superseded it; local composition wins over older external updates. Effective changes publish live, with a final flush on editor disposal; there is no save debounce. Local simulated composition cannot establish every device IME's behavior.

The visible Edit title lazily requests the editor. Loading keeps the read title with a Spinner and makes no writes. A chunk/engine failure is contained inside the title boundary and offers Retry, leaving application content mounted. Retry creates a fresh lazy attempt; it cannot guarantee recovery from an unavailable asset, cache/network failure or repeating engine error. Invalid saved input warnings and oversized draft errors are separate from load errors; application rendering errors are not hidden by a shell-wide boundary.

### Sample and verification limits

The actual sample root uses the shell, manifest defaults, searchable metadata and a show-title pane toggle. Its lazy **WebPartShell** panel makes appearance, Card size, title position, surfaces/padding, inherited host theme/direction, property replacement and visibility observable. Its note/counter show retained body state or the documented structural reset. After hiding the header action, restore visibility using the body Show title switch or existing pane toggle. Dedicated browser fixtures cover native ref, event and style forwarding. Build the library before the app and restart an active serve after library changes. See [development checks](../development/verification.md#sample-and-component-checks) and the [authenticated checklist](../development/sharepoint-validation/INDEX.md#focus-input-and-accessibility).

Local Chrome checks target both source and compiled-library fixtures. Build matching Shell-only bundles first, then run the dedicated checkers:

```bash
npm run build:library
SX_BROWSER_SHELL_ONLY=1 node tests/browser/build/build-sx-browser-fixture.cjs
STYLES_PANEL_SHELL_ONLY=1 node tests/browser/build/build-styles-panel-browser.cjs
node tests/browser/check/check-title-toolbar-localization-browser.cjs
node tests/browser/check/check-title-toolbar-geometry-browser.cjs
```

Both checkers own allocated loopback servers and accept `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE_PATH` (default `playwright`). The [localization checker](../../tests/browser/check/check-title-toolbar-localization-browser.cjs) accepts `SX_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` (default macOS Google Chrome); `TITLE_LOCALIZATION_EVIDENCE` overrides `.docs/maintenance/title-toolbar-localization/browser`. Leave `TITLE_LOCALIZATION_SKIP_CATALOGS` unset for all 50 catalogs. The [geometry checker](../../tests/browser/check/check-title-toolbar-geometry-browser.cjs) uses `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome` directly, including disposable native-zoom profiles; `TITLE_TOOLBAR_EVIDENCE` overrides `.docs/maintenance/title-toolbar-localization/geometry`. Leave `TITLE_TOOLBAR_SKIP_LEGACY` and `TITLE_TOOLBAR_RESET_ONLY` unset for its complete scope. Each directory receives `report.json` (including reached checks on failure) and screenshots. Inspect process exit and diagnostics; a partial report is not full acceptance. Rebuild after changes, and follow [fixture prerequisites and evidence policy](../development/verification.md#focused-manual-fixtures).

The localization checker checks the 50 UI catalogs, color tooltips, instance isolation and narrow/RTL layouts; the geometry checker checks foreground rendering, whole-title formatting, overflow, themes, forced colors and native 200% zoom. These fixtures mount real providers/hooks with service doubles; composition events use CDP and paste uses a synthetic ClipboardEvent, alongside actual mouse/keyboard interactions. They establish local behavior, not authenticated host save/reload/search, live Teams/Office/Outlook behavior, device IME, touch or screen-reader acceptance. Those checks remain NOT EXECUTED until their own host observations are recorded. Catalog completeness and localized UI bindings do not establish native-speaker certification of the translations.

### Header action slot

`action` accepts string/JSX shorthand or a fixed `div` props object under the existing SPFx and Fluent providers. Shorthand keeps its existing DOM; object refs target an inner action div, separate from the shell root. Native attributes, className, consumer style and Fluent render callbacks are supported with the existing peer dependencies:

#### Customize the header action and restore a hidden title

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import * as ReactDom from 'react-dom';
import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import { WebPartShell, useSPFxProperties, type IWebPartShellProperties } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
function HideTitle() {
  const { setProperties } = useSPFxProperties<IWebPartShellProperties>();
  return <button type="button" onClick={() => setProperties({ showTitle: false })}>Hide title</button>;
}
function ShowTitle() {
  const { setProperties } = useSPFxProperties<IWebPartShellProperties>();
  return <button type="button" onClick={() => setProperties({ showTitle: true })}>Show title</button>;
}
export default class HeaderActionWebPart extends BaseClientSideWebPart<IWebPartShellProperties> {
  private readonly actionRef = React.createRef<HTMLDivElement>();
  public render(): void {
    ReactDom.render(<WebPartShell instance={this} action={{ ref: this.actionRef,
      children: (Component, props) => <Component {...props}><HideTitle /></Component>,
    }}><ShowTitle /><p>Body state belongs to the application.</p></WebPartShell>, this.domElement);
  }
  protected onDispose(): void { ReactDom.unmountComponentAtNode(this.domElement); }
}
```

When showTitle is true, an empty props object requests the action container. `showTitle=false` suppresses the entire header regardless of the action value; callbacks are not evaluated and actions are unmounted. Booleans, undefined and legacy null suppress action content. Callbacks execute only during visible rendering, may run more than once, and are never invoked for presence inspection. Static strings are literal. `as` can only repeat div; raw HTML and unsupported native keys are discarded. JSX/callback subtrees remain caller-owned, and React 17 erased `ReactNode` types can bypass literal-object restrictions. Appearance/position do not change the persisted title protocol or provider ownership; their mount boundaries are documented above.

[View public source](../../packages/spfx-react-toolkit/src/controls/web-part-shell/index.ts)

### Reusing formatted regions

The Shell-owned title delegates to [EditableText](../api/controls/editable-text.md), using the same HTML protocol and localized editor. For another independent formatted block in Shell children, render EditableText and persist its HTML/plain text through caller-side `useSPFxProperties`; the guide shows the real hook signatures. The generic control owns a block-capable div and does not fit arbitrary inline action/label/trigger slots. Shell title metadata, property authority and provider behavior remain Shell concerns.

## Complete editing recipes

#### Control a project summary and preserve plain text

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import {
  EditableText, type EditableTextProps,
  type EditableTextBlock, type EditableTextChangeData,
} from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/editable-text';

const headings: readonly EditableTextBlock[] = ['h2', 'h3', 'h4'];

export function ProjectSummary(): React.ReactElement {
  const [html, setHTML] = React.useState<string>();
  const [text, setText] = React.useState('Project summary');
  const [editing, setEditing] = React.useState(false);
  const root = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); // React 17 ref initializer
  const change = (data: EditableTextChangeData): void => {
    setHTML(data.html);
    setText(data.text);
  };
  const props: EditableTextProps = {
    mode: editing ? 'edit' : 'read', value: html,
    fallbackText: 'Project summary', allowedBlocks: headings,
    'aria-label': 'Project summary', 'aria-describedby': 'summary-help',
    onChange: change, strings: { bold: 'Strong', colorNames: { red: 'Danger' } },
  };
  return <section>
    <button type="button" onClick={() => setEditing(value => !value)}>Toggle editing</button>
    <p id="summary-help">One heading; Enter inserts a hard break.</p>
    <EditableText {...props} ref={root} data-project-summary="" />
    <output>{text}</output>
  </section>;
}
```

#### Render saved semantic theme color

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { EditableText } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/editable-text';

// The saved semantic green follows the active theme; its UI name is translated.
const savedHTML = '<h2><span class="wps-color-green">Project documents</span></h2>';

export function ProjectHeading(): React.ReactElement {
  return <EditableText value={savedHTML} />;
}
```

#### Persist HTML and searchable text through SPFx properties

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import {
  EditableText, useSPFxProperties, useSPFxDisplayMode,
  type IWebPartShellProperties,
} from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

interface Properties extends IWebPartShellProperties {
  summary: string;
  summaryHTML?: string;
}

export function SummaryContent(): React.ReactElement {
  const { properties, setProperties } = useSPFxProperties<Properties>();
  const { isEdit } = useSPFxDisplayMode();
  return <EditableText mode={isEdit ? 'edit' : 'read'}
    value={properties?.summaryHTML} fallbackText={properties?.summary ?? ''}
    allowedBlocks={['p']} aria-label="Project summary"
    onChange={data => setProperties({ summaryHTML: data.html, summary: data.text })} />;
}
```

## Observe the actual Shell presentation lifecycle

The test web part exposes three source-owned **WebPartShell** scenarios under **Controlli**. They receive a presentation port for the existing outer Shell and use its initialized provider; copying them into another host requires the same port shape. They never render a second Shell. Choose **Use Card baseline** explicitly before testing Card retention. Title position, visibility, Card size and changes between non-subtle Card appearances retain the note and counter. Switching between subtle and Card can remount that content; the explorer keeps its group, feature and scenario selection above the Shell.

Presentation presets are explicit commands, so selecting a scenario preserves the current outer presentation. **Ripristina scenario** applies the selected source baseline and resets the local values owned by that scenario. Only **Configure the actual web part Shell** owns title commands and restores the persisted title to `SPFx React Toolkit`, and only on explicit reset in actual native Edit mode. The retention and remount scenarios preserve all persisted title properties in Read and Edit. Mount and selection never reset the title. The configuration scenario provides an always-reachable **Show title** command and moves focus there only when a visible header becomes hidden; mounting an already-hidden title preserves navigation focus.

#### Configure the actual web part Shell

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button, Field, Select, Switch } from '@fluentui/react-components';
import { useSPFxProperties, useSPFxDisplayMode, useSPFxFluent9ThemeInfo, type IWebPartShellProperties, type WebPartShellProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

interface DemoRegions {
  controls?: React.ReactNode;
  commands?: React.ReactNode;
  status?: React.ReactNode;
  diagnostics?: React.ReactNode;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
}
function standalone(regions: DemoRegions): React.ReactElement {
  return <div>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</div>;
}
interface DemoShellPort {
  presentation: Required<Pick<WebPartShellProps<IWebPartShellProperties>, 'appearance' | 'size' | 'titlePosition' | 'padding'>> &
    Pick<WebPartShellProps<IWebPartShellProperties>, 'surface' | 'dir' | 'strings' | 'titleEditorStrings' | 'action'>;
  updatePresentation(patch: Partial<DemoShellPort['presentation']>): void;
}
// This module-level action captures no scenario controller or local state.
// A chosen action remains actual Shell presentation until explicitly changed.
function HeaderAction(): React.ReactElement {
  const { properties, setProperties } = useSPFxProperties<IWebPartShellProperties>();
  return <Button size="small" data-shell-demo="action" onClick={() => setProperties({ showTitle: !(properties?.showTitle ?? true) })}>
    {properties?.showTitle === false ? 'Show title' : 'Hide title'}
  </Button>;
}
function actionKind(action: DemoShellPort['presentation']['action']): 'default' | 'ordinary' | 'slot' {
  if (action === undefined) return 'default';
  return action && typeof action === 'object' && 'children' in action && typeof action.children === 'function' ? 'slot' : 'ordinary';
}
interface DemoProps {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  shell?: DemoShellPort;
}

// The host supplies its existing Shell and initialized SPFx provider, never a nested Shell.
export function Demo({ render = standalone, resetRevision = 0, shell }: DemoProps = {}): React.ReactElement {
  return shell === undefined
    ? <p>This scenario requires the actual WebPartShell host, its presentation port and initialized SPFx provider.</p>
    : <ShellContent render={render} resetRevision={resetRevision} shell={shell} />;
}
function ShellContent({ render, resetRevision, shell }: {
  render: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision: number;
  shell: DemoShellPort;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const { properties, setProperties } = useSPFxProperties<IWebPartShellProperties>();
  const { isEdit } = useSPFxDisplayMode();
  const { teamsTheme } = useSPFxFluent9ThemeInfo();
  const showButton = React.useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null); // React 17 ref interoperability requires null.
  const revision = React.useRef(resetRevision);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    // Mount and native Read/Edit updates only observe the revision. A later
    // revision is an explicit reset; no persisted properties are written on mount.
    if (revision.current === resetRevision) return;
    revision.current = resetRevision;
    shell.updatePresentation({ appearance: 'subtle', size: 'medium', titlePosition: 'outside', padding: 'auto',
      surface: undefined, dir: undefined, strings: undefined, titleEditorStrings: undefined, action: undefined });
    if (isEdit) setProperties({ title: 'SPFx React Toolkit', titleHTML: undefined, showTitle: true });
  }, [resetRevision, shell, isEdit, setProperties]);
  const showTitle = properties?.showTitle ?? true;
  const previousShowTitle = React.useRef(showTitle);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    const becameHidden = previousShowTitle.current && !showTitle;
    previousShowTitle.current = showTitle;
    if (becameHidden) showButton.current?.focus();
  }, [showTitle]);
  return <div data-shell-demo="panel">{render({
    controls: <>
      <Field label="Appearance"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'appearance' } }} aria-label="Appearance" value={shell.presentation.appearance}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ appearance: event.target.value === 'filled' ? 'filled' : event.target.value === 'filled-alternative' ? 'filled-alternative' : event.target.value === 'outline' ? 'outline' : 'subtle' })}>
        <option value="subtle">Subtle</option><option value="filled">Filled</option><option value="filled-alternative">Filled alternative</option><option value="outline">Outline</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Card size"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'card-size' } }} aria-label="Card size" value={shell.presentation.size}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ size: event.target.value === 'small' ? 'small' : event.target.value === 'large' ? 'large' : 'medium' })}>
        <option value="small">Small</option><option value="medium">Medium</option><option value="large">Large</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Title position"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'title-position' } }} aria-label="Title position" value={shell.presentation.titlePosition}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ titlePosition: event.target.value === 'inside' ? 'inside' : 'outside' })}>
        <option value="outside">Outside</option><option value="inside">Inside</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Spacing"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'padding' } }} aria-label="Spacing" value={shell.presentation.padding}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ padding: event.target.value === 'none' ? 'none' : event.target.value === 'small' ? 'small' : event.target.value === 'medium' ? 'medium' : event.target.value === 'large' ? 'large' : 'auto' })}>
        <option value="auto">Auto</option><option value="none">None</option><option value="small">Small</option><option value="medium">Medium</option><option value="large">Large</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Surface"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'surface' } }} aria-label="Surface" value={shell.presentation.surface ?? 'auto'}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ surface: event.target.value === 'section' ? 'section' : event.target.value === 'application' ? 'application' : undefined })}>
        <option value="auto">Auto</option><option value="section">Section</option><option value="application">Application</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Switch label="Show title" input={{ as: 'input', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'show-title' } }} checked={showTitle} onChange={(_event, data) => setProperties({ showTitle: data.checked })} />
    </>,
    commands: <>
      <Button onClick={() => setProperties({ showTitle: false })}>Hide title</Button>
      <Button ref={showButton} onClick={() => setProperties({ showTitle: true })}>Show title</Button>
      <Button data-shell-demo="plain" disabled={!isEdit} onClick={() => { if (isEdit) setProperties({ title: 'Project documents', titleHTML: undefined }); }}>Plain title</Button>
      <Button data-shell-demo="rich" disabled={!isEdit} onClick={() => { if (isEdit) setProperties({ title: 'Project documents', titleHTML: '<h2><strong>Project</strong> documents</h2>' }); }}>Formatted title</Button>
      <Button data-shell-demo="empty" disabled={!isEdit} onClick={() => { if (isEdit) setProperties({ title: '', titleHTML: '' }); }}>Empty title</Button>
    </>,
    status: <div role="status" aria-live="polite"><p>Mode: {isEdit ? 'Edit' : 'Read'}</p>
      <p>Presentation choices, dictionaries and the stateless header action persist until explicitly changed, including after scenario departure. Use the actual host title and header action. Presentation presets are explicit; Reset restores this source baseline and restores the title only in Edit.</p></div>,
    diagnostics: <>
      <p data-shell-demo="ui-culture">Native SPFx resource labels with independent title naming and editor overrides. Changes retain the live title and do not save properties.</p>
      <Switch label="Custom title naming" input={{ as: 'input', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'strings' } }} checked={shell.presentation.strings !== undefined}
        onChange={(_event, data) => shell.updatePresentation({ strings: data.checked ? { titleEditorLabel: 'Project section heading', titlePlaceholder: 'Add a project heading' } : undefined })} />
      <Switch label="Custom editor labels" input={{ as: 'input', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'title-editor-strings' } }} checked={shell.presentation.titleEditorStrings !== undefined}
        onChange={(_event, data) => shell.updatePresentation({ titleEditorStrings: data.checked ? { bold: 'Strong', formattingControls: 'Project heading controls', colorNames: { red: 'Alert red' } } : undefined })} />
      <Field label="Direction"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'direction' } }} aria-label="Direction" value={shell.presentation.dir ?? 'host'}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ dir: event.target.value === 'ltr' ? 'ltr' : event.target.value === 'rtl' ? 'rtl' : undefined })}>
        <option value="host">Host</option><option value="ltr">LTR</option><option value="rtl">RTL</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Header action"><Select select={{ as: 'select', ...{ 'data-shell-demo': 'action-slot-toggle' } }} aria-label="Header action"
        value={actionKind(shell.presentation.action)}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ action: event.target.value === 'ordinary' ? <HeaderAction /> : event.target.value === 'slot' ? {
          'data-shell-demo': 'action-slot', children: (Component, slotProps) => <Component {...slotProps}><HeaderAction /></Component>,
        } : undefined })}>
        <option value="default">Default host action</option><option value="ordinary">Ordinary action</option><option value="slot">Callback action slot</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <output data-shell-demo="observations">{JSON.stringify({ mode: isEdit ? 'Edit' : 'Read', teamsTheme, title: properties?.title, titleHTML: properties?.titleHTML,
        showTitle: properties?.showTitle, appearance: shell.presentation.appearance, size: shell.presentation.size, titlePosition: shell.presentation.titlePosition,
        padding: shell.presentation.padding, surface: shell.presentation.surface ?? 'auto', dir: shell.presentation.dir ?? 'host',
        customNaming: shell.presentation.strings !== undefined, customEditor: shell.presentation.titleEditorStrings !== undefined,
        action: actionKind(shell.presentation.action) })}</output>
    </>,
  })}</div>;
}
export const demo = {
  host: 'webPart', kind: 'snapshot', contentPlacement: 'configuration', hostAdapter: 'webPartShell',
  observe: 'Configure the actual outer Shell. Its title and action are outside this scenario; native Read/Edit comes from SharePoint. Reset writes the source title only in Edit.',
};
```

#### Retain content through Shell presentation changes

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button, Field, Input, Select } from '@fluentui/react-components';
import { useSPFxDisplayMode, useSPFxFluent9ThemeInfo, type IWebPartShellProperties, type WebPartShellProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

interface DemoRegions {
  controls?: React.ReactNode;
  commands?: React.ReactNode;
  status?: React.ReactNode;
  diagnostics?: React.ReactNode;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
}
function standalone(regions: DemoRegions): React.ReactElement {
  return <div>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</div>;
}
interface DemoShellPort {
  presentation: Required<Pick<WebPartShellProps<IWebPartShellProperties>, 'appearance' | 'size' | 'titlePosition' | 'padding'>>;
  updatePresentation(patch: Partial<DemoShellPort['presentation']>): void;
}
interface DemoProps {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  shell?: DemoShellPort;
}

// The host supplies its existing Shell and initialized SPFx provider, never a nested Shell.
export function Demo({ render = standalone, resetRevision = 0, shell }: DemoProps = {}): React.ReactElement {
  return shell === undefined
    ? <p>This scenario requires the actual WebPartShell host, its presentation port and initialized SPFx provider.</p>
    : <ShellContent render={render} resetRevision={resetRevision} shell={shell} />;
}
function ShellContent({ render, resetRevision, shell }: {
  render: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision: number;
  shell: DemoShellPort;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const { isEdit } = useSPFxDisplayMode();
  const { teamsTheme } = useSPFxFluent9ThemeInfo();
  const [note, setNote] = React.useState('Intranet project review');
  const [count, setCount] = React.useState(0);
  const revision = React.useRef(resetRevision);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (revision.current === resetRevision) return;
    revision.current = resetRevision;
    setNote('Intranet project review');
    setCount(0);
    shell.updatePresentation({ appearance: 'outline', size: 'medium', titlePosition: 'outside' });
  }, [resetRevision, shell]);
  const cardReady = shell.presentation.appearance !== 'subtle';
  return render({
    controls: <>
      <Field label="Card appearance"><Select aria-label="Card appearance" disabled={!cardReady}
        value={shell.presentation.appearance === 'subtle' ? 'outline' : shell.presentation.appearance}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ appearance: event.target.value === 'filled' ? 'filled' : event.target.value === 'filled-alternative' ? 'filled-alternative' : 'outline' })}>
        <option value="filled">Filled</option><option value="filled-alternative">Filled alternative</option><option value="outline">Outline</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Card size"><Select aria-label="Card size" disabled={!cardReady} value={shell.presentation.size}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ size: event.target.value === 'small' ? 'small' : event.target.value === 'large' ? 'large' : 'medium' })}>
        <option value="small">Small</option><option value="medium">Medium</option><option value="large">Large</option>
      </Select></Field>
      <Field label="Title position"><Select aria-label="Title position" disabled={!cardReady} value={shell.presentation.titlePosition}
        onChange={event => shell.updatePresentation({ titlePosition: event.target.value === 'inside' ? 'inside' : 'outside' })}>
        <option value="outside">Outside</option><option value="inside">Inside</option>
      </Select></Field>
    </>,
    commands: <Button onClick={() => shell.updatePresentation({ appearance: 'outline' })}>Use Card baseline</Button>,
    status: <div role="status" aria-live="polite"><p>Mode: {isEdit ? 'Edit' : 'Read'} · Child counter: {count}</p>
      <p>Choose Use Card baseline first, then edit the note and counter. Card variants, size, title position and host-owned title visibility preserve content. Reset preserves the persisted title.</p></div>,
    children: <>
      <Input aria-label="Project note" value={note} onChange={(_event, data) => setNote(data.value)} />
      <Button onClick={() => setCount(current => current + 1)}>Increment counter</Button>
    </>,
    diagnostics: <output data-shell-demo="observations">{JSON.stringify({ note, count, teamsTheme, appearance: shell.presentation.appearance, size: shell.presentation.size, titlePosition: shell.presentation.titlePosition, padding: shell.presentation.padding })}</output>,
  });
}
export const demo = {
  host: 'webPart', kind: 'snapshot', contentPlacement: 'configuration', hostAdapter: 'webPartShell',
  observe: 'Choose Use Card baseline, edit the note and increment. Card variants, size, title position and host-owned title visibility retain content. Reset preserves all persisted title properties in Read and Edit.',
};
```

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button, Input } from '@fluentui/react-components';
import { useSPFxDisplayMode, type IWebPartShellProperties, type WebPartShellProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

interface DemoRegions {
  controls?: React.ReactNode;
  commands?: React.ReactNode;
  status?: React.ReactNode;
  diagnostics?: React.ReactNode;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
}
function standalone(regions: DemoRegions): React.ReactElement {
  return <div>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</div>;
}
interface DemoShellPort {
  presentation: Required<Pick<WebPartShellProps<IWebPartShellProperties>, 'appearance' | 'size' | 'titlePosition' | 'padding'>>;
  updatePresentation(patch: Partial<DemoShellPort['presentation']>): void;
}
interface DemoProps {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  shell?: DemoShellPort;
}

// The host supplies its existing Shell and initialized SPFx provider, never a nested Shell.
export function Demo({ render = standalone, resetRevision = 0, shell }: DemoProps = {}): React.ReactElement {
  return shell === undefined
    ? <p>This scenario requires the actual WebPartShell host, its presentation port and initialized SPFx provider.</p>
    : <ShellContent render={render} resetRevision={resetRevision} shell={shell} />;
}
function ShellContent({ render, resetRevision, shell }: {
  render: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision: number;
  shell: DemoShellPort;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const { isEdit } = useSPFxDisplayMode();
  const [note, setNote] = React.useState('Intranet project review');
  const [count, setCount] = React.useState(0);
  const revision = React.useRef(resetRevision);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (revision.current === resetRevision) return;

  return render({
```
